observations: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist used for emergency reversal of opioid overdose.
Naloxone is a short-acting competitive antagonist at opioid receptors, including the mu receptor; it is not an opioid agonist.
Naloxone is metabolized mainly in the liver and has a short duration, so repeat dosing or infusion may be needed after long-acting opioids.
Naloxone reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression but does not reverse benzodiazepine-induced respiratory depression.
Naloxone is clinically used in people with opioid use disorder and is not contraindicated solely because of that history.
